provisions.title: Counted strike (legal strikes)
provisions.body:
During the fights of each category, the number of strikes by the blade of the weapon delivered into the legal strike zone of the opponent’s body is counted.
● A counted strike is considered a strike if it was clear and deliberate, and the opponent failed to counter it effectively with a defensive action.

provisions.title: Prohibited Strike Zones (illegal strikes)
provisions.body: The following zones are “illegal strikes” and will not count for your score. Striking into these zones can result in penalties or disqualification.

provisions.title: Back and Front of the Neck
provisions.body: ● Strikes to the back and front of the neck are prohibited.

provisions.title: Base of Skull
provisions.body: ● The base of the skull is considered a prohibited strike zone, specifically defined as the bottom third of the back of the helmet.

provisions.title: Back of Knee
provisions.body: ● Strikes to the back of the knee are prohibited. No pressure is to be placed on the back of the knee.

provisions.title: Groin and Crotch
provisions.body: ● Strikes to the groin and crotch are prohibited.

provisions.title: Feet and Ankles
provisions.body: ● Strikes to the feet and ankles are prohibited. However, striking the foot is not considered a prohibited strike if the competitor raises their foot while the strike is already occurring.

provisions.title: Unprotected Body Parts
provisions.body: ● Any part of the opponent’s body that has lost itself protection is considered a prohibited strike zone.

provisions.title: Sword and Shield
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal strike zone of the opponent will score:
● Two (2) points:
● Head
● Torso
● One (1) point:
● Legs
● Arms
● Hands

provisions.title: Sword and Buckler
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal strike zone of the opponent will score
● one (1) point.

provisions.title: Polearm
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal strike zone of the opponent will score.
● One (1) point:
● Excluding hands: Zero (0) points if the blow landed on the hands.
● Offensive actions with the haft of the polearm do not score.
● The full length of the cutting edge of the weapon is considered a blade.
● The grip must be held by two (2) hands for the strike to be counted as a point.

provisions.title: Longsword
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal strike zone of the opponent will score.
● Two (2) points (Holding the grip with (2) hands).
● Head
● Torso
● One (1) point
● Arms
● Legs
● Hands
● One (1) point (Holding the grip with one (1) hand).
● All legal striking zones

Sword and buckler:
● A match consists of three (3) rounds of no longer than one (1) minute.
● Each round is continued until one of the competitors has scored five (5) points or the time limit has been reached.
● Max points per round is five (5) or the total of counted strikes.
● There is no break in between rounds.

2.5.2 Polearm | Longsword | Sword and shield
● A fight consists of two (2) rounds of no longer than one (1) minute.
● Break of thirty (30) seconds between rounds.
● If the match ends in a draw, an extra thirty (30) second round is fought to determine the winner.
● Competitor with the highest score will win the round.

Important!
The organizers can change the length of the round, provided this decision is coordinated with the Head Organization and is registered in the Tournament Regulations.

2.6 Win conditions The competitor who meets the criteria (2.6.1). Will win the match.
2.6.1 Match win (criteria)

Sword and buckler
● The competitor who wins two (2) rounds first will win the match.
● A competitor is given a technical win (art.2.7)

Longsword | Sword&Shield | Polearm
● Total score from both rounds (the score must have at least 2 point spread)

2.7 Technical Win “Technical win” is awarded to one (1) of the competitors in the following cases 2.7.1 Withdraw
● Failed to report to the list upon the Head Referee’s call.
● Failed to prepare the equipment within the designated time.
● Withdraws before the match has started.
The competitor who failed to report to the list for the match is penalized by a yellow card. In the case a competitor cannot participate in the competition because of injury or disqualification, their opponent is awarded a technical win.

2.7.2 Injury
● If the opponent cannot continue the match because of an “accidental injury”.
● If the competitor cannot continue the match due to the injury caused by an illegal strike, their opponent receives a penalty of double yellow cards and is banned from further participation in the tournament. The injured competitor is awarded a technical victory. The injured competitor is withdrawn from further matches in this category.

2.7.3 Penalties
● If an opponent gets two (2) Yellow cards (warnings) or Red card (disqualification).
2.7.4 Armor failure
● If the match is impeded due to equipment failure that is impossible to fix within the designated time frame of no more than one (1) minute. Assessment is made by the Knight Marshal (Head Referee).

Points awarded for “technical win” All categories get 10-0, beside buckler 2-0

provisions.title: Authorized Fighting Techniques
provisions.body: These rules aim to define a set of permitted and prohibited actions to ensure the safety of participants while engaging in combat. The guidelines cover striking, grabbing, and various techniques to maintain a fair and controlled environment during the event.

provisions.title: Buckler strikes are permitted with the flat of the buckler
provisions.review_note: numbering skips to 3.1.2 (expected 3.1.1): check the official document for a missing provision

provisions.title: Polearm: Competitor is allowed to strike with a free hand if provided they have a
provisions.body: weapon in the other hand

provisions.title: Strikes are permitted with the blade and the haft of the weapon
Strike Zones
provisions.body: ● Strikes are allowed to any area not mentioned as a prohibited strike zone.

provisions.title: Parry
provisions.body: ● Participants are allowed to parry the opponent’s strikes

provisions.title: Techniques and moves with shields (Buckler,Sword&Shield)
provisions.body:
● Pushing the opponent with the shoulder or the flat of the shield.
● Pushing the blade, shield, armed hand or upper body (above the waistline) of the opponent with the flat or the edge of the shield.
● Using the shield to hook or cover the opponent’s shield.

provisions.title: Techniques and moves (Longsword,Polearm)
provisions.body:
● Pushing the opponent with the blade or arms.
● Pushing off the opponent's arms with your arms.

provisions.title: Weapon-Grabbing
provisions.body:
● Participants are allowed to grab their own weapon (except the blade) with their hands.
● Participants are allowed to trap opponents weapon by shield, buckler and/or arm(not by hands)

provisions.title: Pinned to the List Rail
provisions.body: ● Pinning an opponent to the list is not against the rules; however, if a competitor is pinned against the list rail, the Knight Marshal will call 'Break Fight' and reset the competitors to the center of the list.

provisions.title: Prohibited Fighting Techniques
provisions.body: These rules aim to ensure the safety, fairness, and adherence to a set of standards.

provisions.title: Unlisted Techniques
provisions.body: ● Any actions not listed in section 3 of the rules are prohibited.

provisions.title: Thrusting Actions
provisions.body:
● Any thrusting actions with a weapon.
● Threats of a thrusting action.

provisions.title: Offensive Actions at Prohibited Strike Zones
provisions.body: ● Any offensive actions aimed at the prohibited strike zones.

provisions.title: Striking to Grounded or rising competitors
provisions.body: ● Striking a grounded or rising competitor.

provisions.title: Strikes to Disarmed Opponent
provisions.body: ● Strikes to an opponent who has lost their weapon.

provisions.title: Strikes with head
provisions.body: ● Strikes to an opponent with your head.

provisions.title: Strikes with legs
provisions.body: ● Strikes with feet, shin, and knees are prohibited.

provisions.title: Techniques and Moves
provisions.body: ● Back heels, wrestling throws, and clinching.

provisions.title: Punches and elbow strikes
provisions.body:
● Buckler: reference: 3.1.2 Buckler
● Polearm: reference: 3.1.3 Polearm

provisions.title: Strikes with the pommel or cross guard of the sword
provisions.body: ● Strikes delivered with the pommel or cross guard of the sword.

provisions.title: Grappling
provisions.body:
● Grappling with hands and arms to the opponent’s torso, head, and limbs
● Handholds of the opponent’s sword.

provisions.title: Strikes with the shields
provisions.body: ● Strikes delivered with the edge of the shield are prohibited.

provisions.title: Authorized Equipment
provisions.body: These rules aim to ensure a high standard of authenticity, safety, and historical accuracy in the equipment and conduct of the participants

provisions.title: Technical and Authentic Compliance
provisions.body:
● All equipment must meet Buhurt International technical and authentic requirements.
● Reference ”Weapons requirements” for all the rules.
● Reference “Weapons/Shield Chart” for sizes and weights.

provisions.title: Competitor Eligibility
provisions.body: ● Competitors are not allowed to compete unless they have passed technical and authenticity checks.

provisions.title: Weapon Requirements
provisions.body:
● Weapons must meet the Technical Requirement for Permitted Weapons.
● Low-quality, dirty, rusty, or historically implausible weapons are not allowed.

provisions.title: Footwear
provisions.body: ● Modern boots or medieval shoes with explicitly modern outsoles are not allowed.

provisions.title: Materials
provisions.body:
● Modern adhesive tape, plastic ties, and other visible modern materials are not permitted.
● Textile adhesive tape of neutral colors for kit repair is an exception.

provisions.title: Decorations
provisions.body:
● Slogans and imagery on equipment should be historically plausible and not derogatory.
● No modern equipment or decorations are allowed.

provisions.title: Equipment Changes
provisions.body:
● Participants are allowed to change elements of equipment (armor or weapon) during intervals or due to breakage
● Technical Marshal supervision is required for equipment changes

provisions.title: Management of the competitors
provisions.body: Management of the competitors is conducted in accordance with the Buhurt International Duels Regulations, with penalties that are imposed depending on the situation in the list and competitors’ and marshals’ actions.
